name: Manali
tagline: Mountains, meadows, and magic at every turn

attractions.name: Rohtang Pass
attractions.description: At 3,978 metres on the Pir Panjal Range, Rohtang Pass is the dramatic gateway from the Kullu Valley to the arid Lahaul-Spiti plateau. Even in summer, snow blankets the barren landscape where adventurers zip-line, try skiing, and ride snowmobiles. The pass commands staggering views of the Kullu valley on one side and the stark Chandra River gorge on the other. Entry requires a permit due to ecological sensitivity.
attractions.whyVisit: The most accessible high-altitude snow point near Manali, with sweeping views of two contrasting Himalayan worlds.
attractions.mapsSearch: Rohtang Pass, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Solang Valley
attractions.description: Just 14 km north of Manali, Solang Valley is Himachal Pradesh's premier adventure playground. In summer, the lush bowl of meadows hosts paragliding, zorbing, horse riding, mountain biking, and ropeway rides above the valley floor. In winter it transforms into a ski resort, with ski-lifts operating on the snowfields. The backdrop of Hanuman Tibba peak at 5,928 metres makes every activity feel monumental.
attractions.whyVisit: Manali's most versatile adventure hub, offering both winter skiing and summer adrenaline sports.
attractions.bestTime: December to February for skiing; April to June for summer sports
attractions.mapsSearch: Solang Valley, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
attractions.description: Built in 1553 AD, this pagoda-style wooden temple dedicated to Hadimba Devi — the wife of the Pandava Bhima — stands in a dense cedar forest at the edge of old Manali. The four-tiered roof is sheathed in overlapping wooden shingles, and the doorway is adorned with intricate carvings of animals, deities, and floral motifs. The surrounding deodar forest, thick with ferns and wildflowers, lends it an enchanted atmosphere.
attractions.whyVisit: Manali's most sacred and visually distinctive shrine, set amid a magnificent deodar cedar forest.
attractions.mapsSearch: Hadimba Devi Temple, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India
attractions.imageQuery: Hadimba Devi Temple Manali cedar forest

attractions.name: Old Manali
attractions.description: Across the Manalsu Nullah from the modern town, Old Manali is a village of apple orchards, guesthouses draped in bougainvillea, and a charming Manu Rishi temple. The Manu temple, said to mark the spot where the sage Manu landed after the Great Flood, is one of the few temples dedicated to him in India. The café-lined lanes — including Café 1947 and Bob Dylan's favourite hangouts — pulse with backpacker energy.
attractions.whyVisit: The authentic, laid-back heart of Manali, with apple orchards, bohemian cafés, and the rare Manu temple.
attractions.bestTime: March to June; September to November
attractions.mapsSearch: Old Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India
attractions.imageQuery: Old Manali village cafes apple orchards

attractions.name: Beas River Rafting
attractions.description: The Beas River churns through a spectacular gorge between Manali and Kullu, offering Grade II-IV whitewater rafting across a 14-km stretch. The most popular run descends from Pirdi to Jhiri, passing through rapids named Troll, Double Trouble, and Cobra. Flanked by pine-clad ridges and snow-capped peaks, the run combines adrenaline with some of the most beautiful river scenery in the Himalayan foothills.
attractions.whyVisit: The most thrilling and scenically spectacular whitewater rafting run in Himachal Pradesh.
attractions.bestTime: May to July; September to October
attractions.mapsSearch: Beas River Rafting, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Sissu (Khoksar) and Lahaul Valley
attractions.description: After crossing Rohtang, the Lahaul Valley opens dramatically — a high-altitude desert of silver rivers, glaciers, and mud-coloured mountains dotted with whitewashed Buddhist gompas and flat-roofed stone villages. Sissu village sits at a glacial lake beneath a roaring waterfall and is accessible without a permit via the Atal Tunnel. The 360-degree panorama of the Lahaul peaks from Sissu is among the finest in Himachal Pradesh.
attractions.whyVisit: The most accessible window into the stark, serene world of the Lahaul trans-Himalayan plateau.
attractions.mapsSearch: Sissu, Lahaul Valley, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Manali Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: Covering 31 sq km of dense coniferous and broad-leaf forest above old Manali, this sanctuary shelters Himalayan brown bear, leopard, musk deer, bharal, snow cock, and over 180 bird species. The Jogni Waterfall trail passes through the sanctuary's lower reaches, while experienced trekkers explore the higher alpine zones. Autumn brings extraordinary foliage of chestnut, maple, and oak in shades of amber, gold, and crimson.
attractions.whyVisit: A forested mountain sanctuary above Manali offering wildlife trails and a spectacular waterfall.
attractions.mapsSearch: Manali Wildlife Sanctuary, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Naggar Castle
attractions.description: Built by Raja Sidh Singh of Kullu around 1500 AD and now converted into a heritage hotel, Naggar Castle is constructed in the Himalayan kath-kuni style — alternating layers of stone and cedar beams. The castle overlooks the Beas Valley from a steep hillside above Naggar village, 22 km south of Manali. The adjacent art gallery holds original paintings by Russian painter and philosopher Nicholas Roerich, who lived here for 20 years.
attractions.whyVisit: A 500-year-old castle with Roerich's original Himalayan paintings and the finest valley view between Manali and Kullu.
attractions.bestTime: March to June; September to November
attractions.mapsSearch: Naggar Castle, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Chandrakhani Pass Trek
attractions.description: The three-day trek from Naggar village over the Chandrakhani Pass (3,660 m) to the Malana valley traverses dense forest, flower-filled alpine meadows, and a high pass with a peerless panorama of the Kullu valley and Deo Tibba massif. The route connects to Malana, home to an ancient Aryan community that has maintained social isolation for centuries and claims descent from Alexander's soldiers.
attractions.whyVisit: A perfect three-day high-altitude trek combining alpine scenery with access to Malana's enigmatic ancient culture.
attractions.bestTime: May to June; September to October
attractions.mapsSearch: Chandrakhani Pass, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Atal Tunnel (Rohtang Tunnel)
attractions.description: At 3,060 metres, the 8.8-km-long Atal Tunnel is the world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet. Inaugurated in 2020, it ends Lahaul's annual six-month isolation from the rest of Himachal Pradesh. The north portal opens dramatically into the wide, glacier-fed Sissu plain. The tunnel itself, with its controlled lighting and emergency bays, is an engineering marvel carved through the Pir Panjal Range.
attractions.whyVisit: A world-record engineering feat that connects two completely different Himalayan worlds year-round.
attractions.mapsSearch: Atal Tunnel, Rohtang, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Jogni Waterfall
attractions.description: A 5-km forest trail from Old Manali through the wildlife sanctuary leads to the tiered Jogni Waterfall, which drops 30 metres in a series of cascades through moss-covered rocks into a deep pool. The route through apple orchards and deodar forest passes the small Chandra Nahan stream and a photogenic wooden footbridge. The falls are at their most thunderous in June-July after snowmelt.
attractions.whyVisit: The most rewarding short trek from Manali, through forest and orchards to a beautiful multi-tiered waterfall.
attractions.mapsSearch: Jogni Waterfall, Old Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Vashisht Hot Springs and Temple
attractions.description: The ancient stone village of Vashisht, 3 km from Manali, harbours two of the most sacred sulphur hot springs in Himachal Pradesh. The springs feed segregated bathing pools maintained by the village. Adjacent twin temples — one to Rama, one to the sage Vashisht — are elaborately carved in traditional Kath-Kuni woodwork. Bathing in the sulphurous waters is said to cure skin ailments and is a cherished ritual for pilgrims.
attractions.whyVisit: Sacred natural hot springs in a beautifully carved medieval temple village above the Beas River.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; winter for the warming springs
attractions.mapsSearch: Vashisht Hot Springs, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Kullu Dussehra Festival
attractions.description: While the rest of India wraps up Dussehra, Kullu valley's 7-day international celebration begins. Over 200 local deities (devtas) are brought from their villages on decorated palanquins and rathas in a spectacular procession to the Dhalpur Maidan in Kullu, 40 km south of Manali. The festival involves traditional music, folk dances, and local crafts fairs. It is listed as one of India's National Festivals.
attractions.whyVisit: India's most extraordinary post-Dussehra festival, uniting over 200 deities in a unique Himalayan celebration.
attractions.mapsSearch: Kullu Dussehra, Dhalpur Maidan, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Hampta Pass Trek
attractions.description: The 4-day Hampta Pass trek (4,270 m) is one of the most dramatically varied treks in the Indian Himalaya. Starting in the lush green meadows of the Kullu valley, it crosses the pass into the austere lunar desert of Lahaul's Chandra valley — a transformation so complete it feels like crossing to another planet. The meadow of Chika and the cliff-flanked Jwara camp are breathtakingly scenic.
attractions.whyVisit: The most dramatic landscape transition in the Himalaya, from green valley to moonscape desert in one pass crossing.
attractions.mapsSearch: Hampta Pass Trek, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Malana Village
attractions.description: Perched high in a sealed side valley of the Kullu district, Malana is one of the world's oldest direct democracies, governed by its own parliament (Jamdagni Rishi's court) for centuries. The villagers, who claim Aryan descent, maintain strict social codes including prohibitions on outsiders touching their walls or temples. The village architecture, festivals, and unique dialect (Kanashi) form a cultural island unlike anything else in India.
attractions.whyVisit: One of the world's oldest self-governing communities, preserving an ancient Aryan culture in strict isolation.
attractions.mapsSearch: Malana Village, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Rohtang Glacier Trek
attractions.description: Beyond the main Rohtang Pass viewpoint, a trail leads across moraines to the snout of the Rohtang Glacier, the source of the Beas River. The route traverses a moonscape of polished rock, blue ice, and glacial lakes below the Shitidhar peak. The experience of walking on the glacier ice, tracing the river to its birthplace, and surveying the Himalayan panorama from the glacier's edge is profoundly raw and memorable.
attractions.whyVisit: Walk to the glacial source of the Beas River on a raw Himalayan ice-field above the famous pass.
attractions.mapsSearch: Rohtang Glacier, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Bhrigu Lake Trek
attractions.description: The Bhrigu Lake trek (4,300 m) above Gulaba village is one of Manali's finest short treks, taking 2-3 days through a succession of flower-blanketed alpine meadows (bugyals) to a high-altitude lake sacred to Sage Bhrigu. The meadows are among the richest in the Himalaya, carpeted with primulas, blue poppies, and edelweiss. The lake remains frozen until July and mirrors the surrounding snow peaks with mirror-like clarity.
attractions.whyVisit: One of the most colourful high-altitude meadow treks in the Himalaya, culminating at a sacred glacial lake.
attractions.mapsSearch: Bhrigu Lake Trek, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Arjun Gufa (Arjuna's Cave)
attractions.description: Hidden in the forest above Prini village, 7 km south of Manali, this ancient natural cave is believed to be the cave where the Pandava prince Arjuna meditated to obtain the Pashupatastra weapon from Lord Shiva. The cave sits beside a rushing stream in dense deodar forest. Few tourists find it, making the experience of sitting in the smoke-blackened stone chamber, lit only by butter lamps, remarkably authentic.
attractions.whyVisit: A little-visited cave shrine of deep Mahabharata significance, hidden in pristine forest above the Beas.
attractions.mapsSearch: Arjuna's Cave, Prini, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Tirthan Valley
attractions.description: South of Kullu, the Tirthan River carves a pristine valley that forms the buffer zone of the Great Himalayan National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site). Crystal-clear water, trout fishing, waterfalls, and walking trails through mixed oak-rhododendron forest make it Himachal's most serene nature escape. Guesthouses perched on boulders above the river and the absence of vehicles above Gushiani complete a perfect off-grid retreat.
attractions.whyVisit: Himachal's most pristine river valley, a UNESCO buffer zone ideal for trout fishing and forested walking trails.
attractions.bestTime: April to June; September to November
attractions.mapsSearch: Tirthan Valley, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Great Himalayan National Park
attractions.description: This UNESCO World Heritage Site covers 754 sq km of Western Himalayan high-alpine wilderness above Kullu. It shelters the western Himalayan tahr, snow leopard, Himalayan brown bear, musk deer, and over 375 bird species including the western tragopan (Himachal's state bird). The park has no roads — entry is only on foot, making encounters with wildlife and pristine forest completely authentic.
attractions.whyVisit: A UNESCO-listed wilderness park accessible only on foot, sheltering some of the rarest fauna in the Himalaya.
attractions.bestTime: May to June; September to October
attractions.mapsSearch: Great Himalayan National Park, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India
attractions.imageQuery: Great Himalayan National Park trek Kullu

attractions.name: Pin Parvati Pass Trek
attractions.description: One of the Himalaya's most challenging crossings, the Pin Parvati Pass (5,319 m) connects the lush Parvati Valley near Kasol with the arid Pin Valley in Spiti. The 10-day route traverses permanent snowfields, glaciated moraines, and an extremely technical final ascent. The reward is a crossing between two utterly different Himalayan ecosystems — Kullu's green forested valleys and Spiti's Tibetan plateau.
attractions.whyVisit: The most technically demanding and scenically epic high pass crossing in Himachal Pradesh.
attractions.mapsSearch: Pin Parvati Pass Trek, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India
attractions.imageQuery: Pin Parvati Pass glacier trek Himachal

attractions.name: Kasol and Parvati Valley
attractions.description: The Parvati River valley, southeast of Kullu, is one of India's most beautiful Himalayan corridors. Kasol village, a haven for Israeli travellers, sits at the valley's lower end surrounded by pine forests and the roaring green Parvati. Further upstream, Kheerganga's natural hot springs are reached via a stunning 12-km trek through waterfalls and forest. The valley's charming Israeli-influenced cafés, trance music, and riverside camping have earned it the nickname 'Mini Israel'.
attractions.whyVisit: Himachal's most beloved backpacker valley, with hot springs, pine forests, and some of India's finest short treks.
attractions.bestTime: March to June; September to November
attractions.mapsSearch: Kasol, Parvati Valley, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Deo Tibba Base Camp Trek
attractions.description: The 8-day Deo Tibba Base Camp trek (4,350 m) from Jagatsukh village near Manali is one of the finest high-altitude treks in Himachal, passing through the Khanol meadows and the dramatic Chandrakhani La shoulder. The base camp sits in a boulder-strewn amphitheatre beneath the 6,001-metre Deo Tibba peak and its hanging glaciers. On clear days, the panorama stretches from the Lahaul peaks to the Dhauladhar range.
attractions.whyVisit: One of Manali's finest multi-day treks, with outstanding alpine meadows and a dramatic glaciated peak base camp.
attractions.mapsSearch: Deo Tibba Base Camp, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India
attractions.imageQuery: Deo Tibba Base Camp trek Manali

attractions.name: Bijli Mahadev Temple
attractions.description: Atop a 2,460-metre forested ridge 10 km from Kullu, Bijli Mahadev (Lightning Shiva) is one of the most revered Shiva temples in Himachal Pradesh. The 20-metre staff atop the temple is said to attract lightning strikes, which shatter the Shivalingam. Priests then reassemble it with butter and sawdust — symbolising Shiva's self-renewal. The panoramic view of the Kullu valley and Beas River from the ridge is outstanding.
attractions.whyVisit: A mystical hilltop Shiva temple where lightning ritually shatters and renews the sacred lingam each monsoon.
attractions.mapsSearch: Bijli Mahadev Temple, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India

attractions.name: Chhika and Sethan Meadows
attractions.description: Hidden above the Hampta village trail, Chhika and Sethan are a pair of high-altitude meadows accessible in under two hours from the Manali-Leh highway. In summer, the meadows are carpeted with yellow buttercups and blue iris; in winter they transform into a powder-snow backcountry ski playground. The village of Sethan has basic homestays where local Himachali families serve butter tea and hand-rolled chapatis beside wood-burning stoves.
attractions.whyVisit: Manali's closest high-altitude meadow escape, offering wildflowers in summer and powder skiing in winter.
attractions.bestTime: May to June for flowers; December to February for snow
attractions.mapsSearch: Sethan Village, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India
